items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The trumpet section had ... and myself. ... Chester "Butch" Burrell and Herb Fleming, trombones ... Sissle thought he was a singer.

ctx.x: There were fellows in the orchestra that drank and I was advised by a few of them that Sissle didn't like to see them doing it, so when they drank, they did it in an undercover manner. I knew quite a few of the musicians in the band because I had worked with them at one time in other orchestras and on gigs.

The trumpet section had Wendell Culley, Clarence Wheeler, George Wingfield and myself. Ben Whitted, Don Pasquale(altos), Chester "Butch" Burrell and Herb Fleming, trombones, Teddy Giles, bass, Harvey Brooks, piano, Wilbur Kirk, drums, and Olivetto Miller, harp. Sissle thought he was a singer.

I had seen Sissle in some shows that he had been co-produced [of] and in which he had a principal role and although the shows were good and some of them had played in theatres down town, his acting was always corny to me. And as he had no real jazz feeling his type of orchestra was commercial but sad commercial.
